d: The Compliance & Assurance Officer is responsible for supporting the effective implementation of LIVA’s Compliance Framework through independent compliance monitoring, assurance, and advisory activities. The role assists in identifying and assessing compliance risks, evaluating the effectiveness of controls, conducting compliance reviews, monitoring remediation actions, and providing guidance to business stakeholders to ensure compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and internal policies. The role reports directly to the Compliance Director UAE & Bahrain and supports the delivery of the Annual Compliance Plan, regulatory compliance oversight, and compliance risk management activities across the UAE and Bahrain operations. In addition, the role will act as the Deputy Money Laundering Reporting Officer (DMLRO) for Bahrain, supporting the Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO) in the oversight and management of Anti-Money Laundering, Counter-Terrorist Financing, and Sanctions compliance obligations.

The Compliance & Assurance Officer supports the Compliance Director UAE & Bahrain in the oversight and management of compliance and financial crime compliance activities across the UAE and Bahrain operations. The role is responsible for supporting the delivery of the Compliance Monitoring and Assurance Programme, providing compliance advice and oversight, monitoring regulatory compliance obligations, and assisting with the identification, assessment, and reporting of compliance risks and issues. The position also acts as the designated Deputy Money Laundering Reporting Officer (DMLRO) for Bahrain, supporting the MLRO in fulfilling AML, CTF, Sanctions, and Financial Crime regulatory requirements.

We're looking for an Operations Associate to join our team and help solve problems, execute projects, and continuously improve how we operate across Washmen & The Finery. This is a hands-on individual contributor role for someone who is sharp, analytical, hardworking, and hungry to grow. You'll work across different areas of the business, getting into the details of how things work, identifying problems and opportunities, and helping turn ideas into action. You'll also work closely with our Product and Tech teams to help develop systems, features, automations, and AI-enabled solutions that make our operations smarter, faster, and more scalable. You'll report directly to our Operations Director, with close exposure to how decisions are made and problems are solved at the leadership level.
Work on operational projects across Production, Customer Service, Logistics, Product, Tech, Marketing, and other areas of the business.
Investigate operational problems, identify root causes, and develop practical solutions.
Analyze data and performance to identify trends, bottlenecks, and opportunities.
Get close to the operation to understand what's actually happening — not just what the numbers say.
Identify and implement opportunities to improve processes, efficiency, quality, and customer experience.
Work with Product and Tech to translate operational needs into new tools, systems, and product features.
Explore and implement opportunities to use AI and automation to improve workflows, decision-making, productivity, and customer experience.
Build reports and tracking that improve visibility and support better decision-making.
You think well.You can take an unclear problem, break it down logically, ask the right questions, and work your way towards an answer.
You're hungry.You want to learn, improve, take on responsibility, and progress. You're motivated by the opportunity to become better and take on more.
You get things done.You're proactive, organized, and dependable. You take ownership, maintain momentum, and follow through.
You're curious and resourceful.You want to understand why things happen, find the answers you need, and aren't satisfied with surface-level explanations.
You're analytical.You're comfortable working with data, spotting patterns, and using information to make better decisions.

You're comfortable with technology.You're interested in how technology, automation, and AI can solve real business problems. You don't need to be an engineer, but you should be curious about new tools and quick to learn how to use them.
You communicate clearly.You can structure your thinking and communicate it effectively, both verbally and in writing.
You have high standards.You care about the details, take pride in the quality of your work, and don't need to be chased to get things right.
q: 1–4 years of professional experience, ideally in a fast-paced or analytical environment.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
Comfortable working with data and digital tools such as Google Workspace, Notion, Slack, and other business systems.
Able to manage multiple priorities in a fast-moving environment.
Experience in operations, project management, analytics, consulting, startups, scale-ups, technology, or consumer services is a plus.

You become someone we can give a problem to and trust to move it forward. You understand the objective behind the work, investigate problems properly, ask good questions, and bring structure when the answer isn't immediately obvious.
You connect data with what's actually happening on the ground. You don't just identify problems — you help solve them.
You look for ways to use process, technology, automation, and AI to build better solutions rather than simply adding more manual work.
As you grow, the problems we can trust you with become bigger.

Washmen is a fast-growing, technology-enabled services business operating at significant scale in the UAE, with 4 industry-leading facilities totaling over 50,000 sq. ft., a central head office, a fleet of 100 vans, and more than 600 people.

At Washmen, we believe our company is only as good as the people behind it. We look forA players— people who are ambitious, capable, dependable, and hungry to grow. Strong performers are given more responsibility. If you're capable and willing to put in the work, you'll have the opportunity to grow quickly and take on increasingly important problems.

d: Worley is a global company of energy, chemicals and resources experts headquartered in Australia. We partner with our customers to deliver projects and create value across the life of their assets. We specialize in consulting, engineering, procurement and construction across the project lifecycle, with services extending through to operations and decommissioning. Leveraging extensive experience and AI-enabled delivery, we support customers in navigating complexity as they meet today's needs and transition to more sustainable solutions.

The People Advisor is a trusted partner to business leaders and managers, providing strategic and operational people support to enable business performance, workforce effectiveness, and employee engagement. The role acts as the primary people partner to assigned business areas, supporting leaders in workforce planning, organizational effectiveness, talent management, employee relations, performance management, and the execution of people strategies aligned to business priorities.

In addition to its business partnering responsibilities, the role provides day-to-day HR support across the employee lifecycle, including onboarding, employee relations, performance management, talent processes, employee engagement, and HR administration, while ensuring compliance with company policies, procedures, and local labor legislation.

The People Advisor works closely with business leaders, employees, and Centres of Expertise (COEs) to deliver integrated people solutions, implement organizational initiatives, and provide practical, timely guidance on workforce and people matters. The role is expected to build strong stakeholder relationships, influence decision-making, support change initiatives, and contribute to a high-performing, accountable, and engaged workforce.
The position plays a key role in balancing operational excellence with proactive business partnership, ensuring that people decisions support both employee experience and business outcomes.
q: Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Social Sciences, or related discipline preferred.
Minimum 3-5 years of experience in a generalist HR, People Advisor, HR Officer, or HR Coordinator role.
Strong business partnering and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence leaders at all levels.
Commercially aware with the ability to align people strategies to business objectives and operational priorities.
Strong coaching and consulting skills, with the ability to build capability in leaders and managers.
Excellent communication, relationship-building, and interpersonal skills.
Strong employee relations knowledge, including experience managing complex and sensitive people matters.
Sound understanding of local labour laws, employment legislation, and HR governance requirements.
Skilled in organizational design, workforce planning, talent management, and succession planning practices.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret people data and provide meaningful insights and recommendations.
Ability to effectively manage competing priorities and operate in a fast-paced, changing environment.
Strong facilitation, influencing, and change management capabilities.
Ability to manage confidential and sensitive information with professionalism and discretion.
Strong collaboration skills with the ability to work effectively across business functions and Centres of Expertise.
Proficiency in HRIS platforms, workforce analytics, and reporting tools.
Demonstrated ability to challenge constructively and provide balanced, risk-based people advice.
Strong understanding of employee engagement, leadership effectiveness, performance management, and culture initiatives.
Results-oriented with a continuous improvement mindset and focus on driving business outcomes through people solutions.

We want our people to be energized and empowered to drive sustainable impact. So, our focus is on a values-inspired culture that unlocks brilliance through belonging, connection and innovation. We're building a diverse, inclusive and respectful workplace. Creating a space where everyone feels they belong, can be themselves, and are heard.

And we're not just talking about it; we're doing it. We're reskilling our people, leveraging transferable skills, and supporting the transition of our workforce to become experts in today's low carbon energy infrastructure and technology. Whatever your ambition, there's a path for you here.
And there's no barrier to your potential career success. Join us to broaden your horizons, explore diverse opportunities, and be part of delivering sustainable change.
